interview.q1: SYNTHETIC: It is an unofficial news site about Web Summit Lisbon, made by a small team with AI agents. The part that helped me is a practical guide to getting from the airport to the arena; the rest is news, company profiles and some AI-agent questions I did not need.
interview.q2: SYNTHETIC: Dinis Cruz, Indi Gupte and Vicky (Wang, I think), plus a lot of AI agents with email-looking names. The same team works on something called RiskMandate. It says clearly that it is not Web Summit.
interview.q3: SYNTHETIC: For the transport stuff, mostly yes: every time and price had a Web Summit or Metro de Lisboa link read yesterday, and it even listed which official pages are out of date. For the AICEP page, no: it said 'Confirmed: Yes' and '404' and 'No one is listed' at the same time, so I would not plan my day on it. The pounds balance that kept changing also made me a bit wary.
interview.q4: SYNTHETIC: Monday 9 November: land, collect wristband and buy the 23-euro 3-day pass at the Terminal 1 accreditation area (7.30am to 10pm), red line to Oriente. Tuesday 10 at 11am: the first-timers' meetup, if I can find out where it is. Before that, open the official app, because the site itself says times can change.
interview.q5: SYNTHETIC: Maybe, leaning no. A page about my company with every fact sourced and an open 'tell us if it is wrong' is a decent reason to check it, and I like that it says an AI drafted it and a named person sent it. But I am a PM at my first summit, not the person who decides about our AI agents' permissions, and three questions plus a 15-minute meeting from a site 'powered by RiskMandate' reads like a polite sales lead. I would forward it to our CTO or security lead and not reply myself.
interview.q6: SYNTHETIC: Put a 'First time at Web Summit? Start here' card at the very top of the front page that links to the first-day guide and shows Monday to Thursday with where each thing is; and drop or explain the '£5.00' balance.

findings.finding: The 'In short' list answers a first-timer's whole commute in five bullets: where to collect the wristband, Oriente 300 metres from the arena, the Carris shuttle, the 23 / 31.50 euro pass, bring a card.
'What this does not claim' openly flags two out-of-date official pages on the transport pass, which made the article's times more believable, not less.
'Independent. Not affiliated with Web Summit' and 'independent of Web Summit, not of RiskMandate' are stated on the front page, the company page and About, consistently.
The first-day article, the one a first-time attendee needs, is the sixth item in 'Latest', four phone screens down, with no visual weight; the lead slot goes to Brazil's trade mission.

One screen says 'Confirmed for 2026: Yes' naming a speaker, says the session page answered 404 and is left out, and says 'No one is listed' under People, so a reader cannot tell if the masterclass is happening.
The only date and place for AICEP's session ('11 Nov, Masterclasses, Masterclass 3') appears inside a source note, not in the 'At the summit' section at the top.

The '£5.00' pill in the top bar, and the '0.1p of 1p' / 'Balance' box at the end of pages, look like a charge with no explanation; the balance shows £5.00, £4.91, £4.97 and £5.00 across four pages, once going up.
The first-timers' meetup (Tuesday 10 November, 11am to 11.55am) is given a time but no room, stage or link.
The reading meter says 'read 5%' at the bottom of an article the reader scrolled to the end of (and 'read 5%' again at the end of the AICEP page).
Raw source URLs in angle brackets overflow the 390 px screen on the right ('registration/>', 'desdob'), and a repository path 'desks/curator/README.md' is listed among the public sources.
The monospace agent block at the foot of the page is cut off on the right ('PrompTugal__News__Website (', 'not instru') on a phone.
The 'NEWS' tab fades out at the right edge of the top bar and the floating 'Ask' button covers the end of text lines on most screens.
The front-page agenda stops at Sunday 8 November with registration repeated as separate rows; the conference days themselves are only behind 'Every event' or the footer link 'Events, by day'.
An 'OUR PICK' tag sits on a non-Web-Summit side event (Portugal Tech Week Palace) with no reason given.
The count for 'Governance, risk and compliance' wraps as '1' over '5' on a phone.
About names the source code 'SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__Web-Summit' while the AICEP page footer names 'github.com/PrompTugal/PrompTugal__News__Website'.
About lists 'Vicky, editor' without a surname while bylines say 'Vicky Wang', and the agent name 'newsroom@web-summit.dinis' wraps into five broken lines in the table.
'Trade Comissioner' is misspelt in the 'Confirmed for 2026' row.
RiskMandate is named on every page ('Powered by RiskMandate') but no screen Daniel saw says in one plain line what it is.
